verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Florida Senate bill page for HB 1361 (2024), the Senate Education Pre-K-12 Committee's House message summary of 7 Mar 2024 and the House staff final bill analysis, stored from flsenate.gov on 14 Oct 2026 and found unchanged by the archiver on 17 Oct 2026, and stored again for this run, on 17 Oct 2026, the enrolled text of CS/HB 1361 and the page for s. 1002.321 in the 2026 Florida Statutes (flsenate.gov). The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, history and votes, approval by the Governor on 9 May 2024, Chapter No. 2024-162 and the 7/1/2024 effective date; the final analysis confirms approval, chapter and effective date. The enrolled text gives s. 1002.321(3) (grants during the school day and the platform conditions), s. 1004.561(6) (grants and the $2 million recurring appropriation) and the July 1, 2024 effective date; the 2026 statute shows subsection (3) with the same wording, apart from a hyphen ('district- and school-level'), and a history ending with s. 1, ch. 2024-162. Whether s. 1004.561(6) has been amended since 2024 was not checked: its 2026 text was not stored.

changes.verification.note: rewritten for this recheck, with the enrolled text and the 2026 statute now stored for this run; no field of the record changes

judgment.status_reasoning: Approved by the Governor on 9 May 2024 as ch. 2024-162, L.O.F.; Section 10 of the enrolled text says the act takes effect July 1, 2024. The 2026 Florida Statutes still carry s. 1002.321(3) as the act enacted it, with a history ending in s. 1, ch. 2024-162, so no later law has amended or repealed the AI grant conditions. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An education omnibus act whose AI content is a grant programme with conditions on the AI platforms it funds; borderline and included with the existing scope_note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's approval, 9 May 2024; date_in_force is 1 Jul 2024. The chapter number was recorded on 13 May 2024, which is not an adoption date.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The 2026 text of s. 1002.321(3) and the enrolled text support every claim of the current summary: grants for subscription fees and professional learning for grades 6 to 12 during the school day, the platform conditions (GPT-4, its equivalent or a successor on a closed system, one-on-one tutoring aligned to the B.E.S.T. Standards, district- and school-level reporting and parental access to AI interactions) and, in s. 1004.561(6), the Lastinger Center's grants with $2 million in recurring funds. Left unchanged.
